articoli.rubrica: An overview of existing Union-wide assessments coordinated by EBA, EIOPA and
Executive Summary
articoli.testo:
1 Executive Summary
The Joint Monitoring Mechanism (JMM) established under Article 23b of the Regulation (EU)
2024/2987 amending the European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR), acts as a
central body for coordinated, cross-sectoral oversight of the European clearing landscape.
In line with Article 23b(6) of EMIR, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA),
in cooperation with other JMM participating authorities, presents its first annual report
covering the results of the JMM’s activities during its inaugural year of operation in 2025.
A central strand of work has been the development of a monitoring framework for the
implementation of the Active Account Requirement (AAR). This involved identifying relevant
indicators, leveraging existing data, and providing regular updates to inform discussions
during JMM meetings. Early evidence suggests that there has been a moderate but still
limited increase in activity at EU central counterparties (CCPs), particularly among smaller
entities and in certain AAR-related products. However, the systemically important third-
country CCPs (Tier 2 CCPs) continue to dominate clearing in most AAR-related products. It
remains to be seen whether EU entities’ excessive exposures to substantially systemic
important clearing services of Tier 2 CCPs will further decrease in coming months. A final
assessment of the effectiveness of the AAR is expected in 2027.
In parallel, the JMM explored broader cross-border developments beyond the AAR, mainly
the US. The analysis indicates that cross-border interdependencies are a core feature of
global cleared markets. EU entities, primarily banks, have considerable exposures to US
CCPs, while US firms are active participants in EU and Tier 2 CCPs, and provide essential
services such as liquidity, custody, and payments. These linkages reflect both the global
nature of US and EU cleared markets and the international footprint of their participants,
supporting market efficiency, liquidity and risk-sharing, but also creating channels through
which shocks could propagate
The JMM also examined broader trends affecting EU CCPs. Since the implementation of
EMIR, EU CCPs have expanded the range of asset classes and products they clear. At the
same time, risk management practices have evolved, notably through a shift from SPAN
based-models to value-at-risk methodologies. These trends underline the adaptability of EU
CCPs to changing regulatory requirements and market conditions.
Finally, the JMM conducted a stocktaking exercise of existing EU-wide stress test
assessments, with a view to increase awareness within the JMM and explore synergies with
aspects related to the EU clearing ecosystem.
